acceptance.given: Frontmatter input, including malformed or adversarial content, is supplied to the repository frontmatter parser.

oracle.expected: Parsing yields structured data or a controlled validation error without executing YAML constructors, object constructors, arbitrary code, or parser-induced host-process side effects.
forbidden: Any YAML or object constructor executes during parsing.
Parsing side effects alter the host process.
The parser reports success while unsafe execution occurred.
oracle.observable: The focused frontmatter parser test instruments constructor and side-effect counters, invokes the real validator parser, and inspects the parsed result or controlled error together with unchanged counters and process state.

acceptance.then: The parser returns parsed frontmatter data or a validation error, and the safety instrumentation shows no arbitrary execution or host-process side effect.
acceptance.when: During frontmatter parsing and the associated focused safety validation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the focused frontmatter safety selector in scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_core.py and fail when constructor execution, arbitrary code execution, or parser-induced host-process mutation is observed; bind the assertion to scripts/sc/validate_skill_quality.py.

affected_subjects: Frontmatter parser safety for malformed and adversarial frontmatter
slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure frontmatter parsing uses safe data-only parsing and returns parsed data or a controlled validation error without executing constructors or arbitrary code.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert the parser implementation while preserving the existing validator API, result schema, and frontmatter validation behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Frontmatter input moves from supplied/untrusted state to parsed data or a controlled validation-error state with execution counters unchanged.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The focused frontmatter safety selector passes with parsed-data-or-controlled-error behavior and zero constructor or arbitrary-execution side effects.
